days.theme: Down the stone street to the waterfall, then the night circuit once the falls light up
days.why: An 11:30 arrival, cleared 11:45, ~15 min from the station (only ~5 km), checked in and ticketed by ~12:35, rice tofu, free from ~13:15. That is a real afternoon plus a full evening. Daylight block: Wuli Stone Street (60 min) as the orientation spine, Tuwang Palace (30) on the cliff edge above it, then the waterfall and the plank walkway behind the 60 m curtain (60), then the Youshui cruise (30) for the only angle that shows the falls, the stacked town and the reflections in one frame — off the water by ~16:45. Then a genuine 1h15 of nothing before dinner, which an arrival day has earned. Night block starts at 19:30 exactly, because that is both when the illumination comes on and when the free evening Tujia set runs at Baishetang: show 19:30-20:00, Shenpu Camp Square panorama 20:05, far-bank platform for the postcard angle 20:30-21:00. The falls stay lit to ~22:00-22:30, so nothing here is rushed. Stop time 4h20 across an 8h window. The entire night circuit was running in daylight. Baishetang Square is a SHOW, not a square you walk into — sets run ~10:30/11:00/13:00/14:00/15:00/16:00 and then the free evening set at 19:30, and the chain had you arriving 16:55, in the gap between two of them, to an empty stage. It is now held to 19:30, which is also the moment the whole town and the waterfall light up, so Shenpu Camp Square (tagged night) and the Far-bank platform follow it into actual darkness at 20:09 and 20:38 instead of 17:34 and 18:03. Dinner is pulled to 16:30 so it sits after the river cruise and before the lights: you finish eating at 18:24, the town illuminates at 19:30, and you are already out in it. Illumination runs to 22:00-22:30, so the 19:30-21:08 sequence is a floor, not a deadline.
days.cut: Nothing. Furong is small enough that a half-day plus an evening genuinely absorbs seven of its eleven entries.

days.theme: Mist on the Youshui, one relic, a second unhurried pass
days.why: The 13:15 departure with a 45-minute buffer means the station at 12:30 and leaving town at ~12:05 — so this is a full six-hour morning, the opposite of Fenghuang's day 2. Out at 06:00 for mist on the Youshui and empty flagstones (45 min, sunrise ~06:05), back for breakfast, then the Xizhou Bronze Pillar (20 min) — the 940 AD peace-treaty column, deliberately held back to day 2 so the arrival afternoon stays walkable and so the one indoor-ish relic stop is not competing with the waterfall. Then the mop-up (60 min): the behind-the-falls walkway again in morning light with a fraction of yesterday's crowd, and anything on Wuli Street missed at speed. That lands you done by ~09:40 with slack before lunch and the 12:05 departure — intentional. Total stop time 2h05 in a window that could hold four hours; the second day of a two-day stop in a town this size should not be filled just because it can be. Lunch is back. The chain had been dropping it silently: the morning runs out of sights at 08:42 and the old rule only fired a meal already due, so a day whose last activity ended before noon simply never ate before its train. It now waits for the window and eats 11:55-12:55, clear of the 13:15 station call. The 08:42-11:55 gap is genuine free time in a town you can cross in ten minutes — everything researched here is already placed.

ideas.name: Check in at Waterfall Bay
ideas.why: Logistics, not a sight — the hotel block is inserted automatically. Budget 30 min because it is also where you buy the ¥108 ticket, which is valid 2-3 days and covers the waterfall, Tuwang Palace and every Baishetang performance. Booking required; do not schedule anything else until it is done.

notes: Furong is the rare stop where the researched list and the time available actually match — all eleven entries are placed, ten as real stops and one as the hotel block. There is no long drop list here because there is nothing that needs dropping. Contrast Fenghuang, where six of fifteen do not fit.

Baishetang performance times confirmed across multiple guides: daytime sets around 10:30, 11:00, 13:00, 14:00, 15:00 and 16:00, plus an evening show at 19:30 (a second, ticketed theatre show follows at ~20:30). Take the 19:30 free set — it lands exactly with the illumination and costs nothing extra on the ¥108 ticket. If it is cancelled, the 16:00 daytime set is the fallback and slots straight into day 1's dead hour.

Waterfall illumination runs ~19:30 to 22:00-22:30 (the whole town lights at the same time). That gives the night viewpoint circuit about 2.5 hours of runway, so treat the 20:00-21:00 sequence as a floor, not a schedule.

The Youshui cruise is the one unverified item: sources give ~¥100 and describe routes from ~30 min up to a 1 h run past the falls from the Hongshi Forest pier, with no published departure times. It is kept on day 1 afternoon precisely because boats are certainly running then — confirm the schedule at the pier on arrival. If it turns out to be the longer 1 h route, it still fits inside day 1's slack.

Departure arithmetic: 13:15 train − 45 min buffer = station at 12:30; − ~15 min transfer = leave town 12:05. Both hub times are PROVISIONAL. If the departure moves earlier, drop the mop-up first — the dawn session and the bronze pillar are the two that cannot be recovered from day 1.

Everything in this town sits within a few hundred metres, so inter-stop walking is near zero and the timings above are close to pure stop time. That is why a seven-stop arrival day is honest here and would not be in a larger town.
